DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 61 s. 2022 June 30, 2022 LOPE N. TUBERA Bureau of Internal Revenue Revenue District Officer RDO 23B-South Nueva Ecija Dear Mr. Tubera: This has reference to your letter dated 21 February 2022 requesting for guidance in the determination of whether various incomes, such as service, business and miscellaneous or other income are proprietary in character which may be subject to internal revenue taxes in conformity with the NIRC, as amended. At the outset, in as much as we would like to discuss the provisions of law or rules which we reckon to be applicable based on the representations in the letter, we deem it proper to defer to the position of the Department of Finance — Bureau of Local Government Finance (DoF-BLGF) considering that the issue contained herein pertains to the determination of whether various incomes, such as service, business and miscellaneous or other income are proprietary in character, falls squarely under their technical expertise, and its mandate to supervise the revenue operations of all local government units (LGUs) and monitoring of its implementation of policies and measures on local revenue. Be that as it may, it is noteworthy to highlight the dual functions of LGUs as provided under Sec. 15 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), to wit: SECTION 15. Political and Corporate Nature of Local Govemment Units. — Every local government unit created or recognized under this Code is a body politic and corporate endowed with powers to be exercised by it in conformity with law. As such, it shall exercise powers as a political subdivision of the national government and as a corporate entity representinq the inhabitants of its territory. Consistently, the dual nature of an LGU can be correlated with the corporate powers of every LGU under Sec. 22(6) of the LGC which provides that "(e)very local government unit, as a corporation, shall have the power to exercise such other powers as are granted to corporations, subject to the limitations provided in this Code and other laws. " Simply put, the LGU, in its governmental functions, acts as an agent of the State for the government of the territory and the inhabitants. On the other hand, it acts as a "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

separate entity for its own purposes and not as a subdivision of the State. Correspondingly, incomes of LGUs are classified in two main types, revenues; and receipts. Revenues are those related to taxation while receipts are that of non-tax related. In terms of locally sourced income, aside from tax revenues, LGUs also derive income from non-tax receipts from fees and charges, government business operations, and other miscellaneous income. Under non-tax revenues, these include, regulatory fees, service charges, receipts from economic enterprises, toll fees and other receipts. As defined by the DoF-BLGF, regulatory fees are those derived from the exercise of the regulatory powers of LGUs. Service income refer to those reasonable charges for services rendered. Toll fees are those which are derived for the use of a public road, pier or wharf, waterway, bridge or telecommunications system, and receipt from economic enterprises are those imposed for the operation of economic enterprises in connection with the government's exercise of its proprietary functions. Accordingly, we deem it appropriate to identify local economic enterprises as provided under the Department of Budget and Management's Manual on Setting Up and Operation of Local Economic Enterprises, which includes public markets, slaughter houses, hospitals, public cemeteries, parking areas, sports, recreational and cultural facilities, public utilities such as water and power supply and distribution and telecommunications, garbage collection and disposal, and public transport and terminal services, among others. In view of the foregoing, we are of the considered view that those incomes listed under business income in the subject letter are proprietary and may be subject to internal revenue taxes. However, as to those listed under income from service, we aie of the opinion that these income relate to the exercise of regulatory powers of the LGU and are thus, governmental function. Notwithstanding, we would like to reiterate that we defer to the position of the DOF- BLGF and Department of Budget and Management and that this opinion is being issued without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of competent authorities or courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very -respectfully yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: L. IRINGAN, CESO Ill Local Go ment OSEC/EMA/LLl_s-LRALLD/rjki Page 2 of 2
